scenes.headline: How a retriever scores a page token by token
scenes.sub: pplx-embed-v2-late: a vector per token, two sizes, one space
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Mosaic! Here's how Perplexity's new retrievers search pages without squeezing each one into a single vector.

scenes.text: Keep a small vector for every token and image patch, let each query word find its best match, and train two model sizes into one shared space.
scenes.mark: two model sizes into one shared space
scenes.say: Keep a small vector for every word and patch. Let each query word find its best match. And make a big and a small model share one space.

scenes.title: One vector, or one per token

left.title: Dense embedding
left.say: A dense model squeezes a whole page into one vector.

right.title: Late interaction
items: Scored with MaxSim at query time
right.say: Late interaction keeps a small vector per token, and compares them all at query time.

scenes.title: MaxSim: each query token keeps its best match

steps.label: every pair compared
steps.say: Every query token meets every document token: fifteen similarities.

steps.label: best match per row
steps.note: quick to easy, pasta to noodle, recipe to dish
steps.say: Each keeps only its best partner. Pasta picks noodle, recipe picks dish.

scenes.title: The score, term by term
scenes.text: s(q, d) = sum over i of max over j of q_i . d_j

parts.note: the best document token for this query token
parts.say: For each query token, take its best match in the document.

parts.note: a cosine, since every vector is unit length
parts.say: Vectors are unit length, so each match is a cosine.

parts.note: add up the query tokens' best matches
parts.say: Add the best matches up: two point three six.

steps.say: The big model reads each page once, offline, and stores about seventeen hundred small vectors.
Both sizes were distilled from one teacher, token by token, so their vectors share a space.
So the small model can encode live queries cheaply.
MaxSim scores them straight against the big model's pages.
Perplexity compares small with small, small on a big index, and big with big.
On text, the big index lifts small queries about halfway, at no extra query cost.
On page images, a bit less.

scenes.title: Storage for one 150-dpi page
scenes.note: nothing in the release pools or compresses the vectors
scenes.say: The price is storage: about twenty-six times a single wide vector, with no compression shipped.

scenes.text: Index once with the big model and query with the small one: the index costs the same bytes either way.

scenes.say: A vector per token, a best match per word, and a big index searched by a small model.
